name: Nala Sinephro
label: Warp
lede: Nala Sinephro plays pedal harp through modular synths and makes jazz that doesn't follow jazz's rules. Her second album, Endlessness, is ten pieces all called "Continuum", and Pitchfork ranked it fifth of 2024.

eras.title: Brussels to Boston, by way of a harp
eras.text: Born in Brussels to a Belgian piano-teacher mother and a Martinican-Guadeloupean jazz-saxophonist father, Sinephro came to music sideways: biochemistry, then a school with a jazz department, then the pedal harp.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.h: A harp at 16, after violin by ear
years.p: Sinephro grew up outside Brussels, moved from a biochemistry track to an arts high school with a jazz department, and took up the pedal harp.
years.xp:
Wikipedia, citing press profiles, says her mother was a classical piano teacher and her father a jazz saxophonist of Martinican and Guadeloupean descent. It also says she developed a jaw tumor as a teenager and that, after it was removed, she spent a stretch going to Brussels clubs for hardcore dance music.

AllMusic puts her taking up the pedal harp at 16, after learning folk songs on violin by ear. Her time is split in the bio between Belgium and Martinique, where family lives.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Still Listening: Endlessness review
years.p: She left the Boston college after a year, deciding her job as a sound engineer taught her more than the classes did.
years.xp: A second jazz college in London followed, and she dropped out of that one quickly too, according to Wikipedia. The engineering habit stuck: her albums credit her with production, engineering and mixing alongside the playing.

eras.title: North London, and a radio show of her own
eras.text: In London she landed in the scene around Shabaka Hutchings and Nubya Garcia, played in a collective, and spent two years writing the music for her debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.p: She has lived in North London since 2018, playing with the Steam Down improvisation collective and working in the circle of the [[London Contemporary Orchestra|47f3b634-a476-4ca7-930b-5ff9f46b133a]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says the scene around Hutchings and Garcia helped her develop a sense of individuality in her style. AllMusic lists neo-soul singer [[Demae|5323e27d-ea62-4af4-883e-1c33a25f417a]] and LCO conductor [[Robert Ames|1174b084-89ec-47e1-9888-35301673f234]] among her early collaborators.

years.cap: Nala Sinephro performing at the Horniman Museum, London
years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.h: NTS hands her a monthly show
years.p: The program began in June 2020 and gave her a place to play the ambient and spiritual-jazz records she'd absorbed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Beats Per Minute: Endlessness review
years.h: Lockdown in Martinique, with a field recorder
years.p: She spent months on the island where her family lives and got into field recording, which fed the music that followed.

eras.title: Space 1.8
eras.text: Her debut came out on Warp, from sessions recorded years before anyone heard them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Space 1.8 · Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Warp: Space 1.8
years.h: Her debut lands on Warp: eight pieces for harp and modular synth
years.p: Sinephro is joined by a rotating cast including [[Nubya Garcia|42dd1862-7255-47ed-8584-651abce3bf53]] and [[James Mollison|fa407068-5773-4dbe-a34a-6d1917d93fd4]], on tapes made in 2018 and 2019.
years.xp:
Sinephro wrote on piano, recorded pedal harp and modular synth parts at home, then took the material into Pink Bird studio with Garcia, Mollison, drummer Jake Long and bassists Twm Dylan and Wonky Logic, per Wikipedia. Warp lists it as catalog WARPCDD324.

Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and put it at No. 24 on its 50 best albums of 2021, according to Wikipedia. Metacritic scored it 85 from seven critics.

years.big: I reach a trance state. I'm almost sleepwalking.
years.src: The Afterword: Space 1.8 · Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro
years.h: The Guardian asks how she plays harp half asleep
years.p: Nala Sinephro, in a November 2021 profile, on the state her hands work in.
years.xp: The Guardian profile, by Ammar Kalia, ran under that quote. She told the paper she has to surrender to the sound and might hold one note for ten minutes straight if that is what the moment calls for, a line also quoted in The Afterword's write-up. Pitchfork followed with its own profile in January 2022.

eras.title: One cycle, ten Continuums
eras.text: Five years after the tapes, a second album built as a single continuous piece, with a bigger band and a string ensemble.

years.cap: Nala Sinephro live at Flow Festival
years.h: St Ann & the Holy Trinity hears Endlessness in one go
years.p: Her band ran the album through as a single piece in Brooklyn Heights, on modular synth, harp, drums and saxophone.
years.xp: A Black Noise reviewer wrote that the group played with so much restraint that they seemed to be holding space rather than filling it. There was no opener and no drinks, which made the room feel ceremonial.

years.cap: Nala Sinephro live at Pitchfork Music Festival, Union Park, Chicago, July 2024
years.p: The opener is a patient piece built on the arpeggio that runs through all ten tracks.

years.src: Album of the Year: Endlessness · Wikipedia: Endlessness · Still Listening: Endlessness review · Beats Per Minute: Endlessness review
years.h: Pitchfork scores Endlessness 8.5 and ranks it fifth of 2024
years.p: Ten pieces, all called "Continuum", in 45 minutes. Daniel Felsenthal wrote the review.
years.xp:
Sinephro played harp, keys and synths and produced it, with Rick David of Pink Bird as engineer. Players include Garcia and Mollison on saxophone, Morgan Simpson (ex-[[black midi|4afbef0a-05ee-4551-b0e0-f1f1870d8f1c]]) and Natcyet Wakili on drums, [[Sheila Maurice-Grey|2e358555-415c-478b-a0b5-b0b329170028]] on flugelhorn, [[Lyle Barton|cef6431a-9ea3-44f1-bfdc-9d16aae0ed39]] on keys, and Orchestrate's strings. A bass line from Alice Sinephro is sampled on Continuum 4.

Reviewers noted the synths are tuned to 432Hz. Felsenthal called it a "potent and intuitive second album" that imagines a music between ambient and jazz. Metacritic's aggregate was 83, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Nala Sinephro in front of her harp, 2024
years.h: Crack puts it third, The Line of Best Fit sixth
years.p: Paste ranked Endlessness tenth, and Bleep, Uncut, Exclaim! and Rough Trade also ran it on their year-end lists.

eras.title: The Smashing Machine
eras.text: A film director heard Endlessness and handed her a movie.

years.cap: Nala Sinephro live at the Berliner Philharmonie, October 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: The Smashing Machine · Resident Advisor: The Smashing Machine
years.h: Benny Safdie hears Endlessness and calls her about a film
years.p: Safdie hired her for The Smashing Machine, his A24 film about MMA fighter Mark Kerr, played by Dwayne Johnson. It's her first film score.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smashing Machine · Resident Advisor: The Smashing Machine
years.p: Warp and A24 Music release it October 3, the day the film opens, with Garcia, Mollison and Morgan Simpson back in the room; vinyl follows January 23, 2026.
years.xp: Reviews split. Pitchfork praised its "disarmingly rich, romantic sweep"; Rolling Stone found it "woozy" and at times soporific, and the Wall Street Journal called it jagged and discordant, per Wikipedia's summary.
